title: Reading Drill — Comparing labels on an herb trail — A pilot study
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing labels on an herb trail — A pilot study
passages.body:
**A** A project in Bramley began with reports of visitors mixing up plants with similar leaves. The garden educator had heard several complaints, but individual reports could not show how often the problem occurred. The team collected evidence using visitor worksheets and chose correct identifications as its main measure. That allowed it to compare different days using the same rule.

**B** The proposed response was side-by-side drawings. Rather than apply it immediately across the whole site, the team ran a trial in a single area. The trial lasted three weeks. A second area kept its previous arrangements, making it possible to see whether any change occurred at both sites.

**C** The first review recorded plants not in bloom as a factor that could affect the comparison. The team advised repeating the study under different conditions before drawing a wider conclusion. It kept the evidence from the first trial but published a note about why the figures might not apply elsewhere.
